Dette ligger i hjerte af den igangværende debat inden for psykedelisk medicin om hvad der egentlig driver helbredelse. Nogle forskere understreger stoffets farmakologiske kraft, mens andre fremhæver betydningen af 'set og setting'—psykologisk forberedelse og miljøkontekst. Dette studie antyder, at begge betyder noget, men måske ikke på den ligetil måde, mange antog. Det indikerer, at god terapeutisk støtte kan virke mindre ved direkte at trøste patienter og mere ved at skabe betingelser, hvor medicinen selv kan virke mere fuldt ud. Efterhånden som psykedelika nærmer sig klinisk tilgængelighed, hjælper disse indsigter med at præcisere hvilke former for faglig uddannelse og omsorgsmæssige strukturer der betyder mest og besvarer en ægte mangel i vores forståelse.

items.title: Multi-metric evaluations of acute psychedelic effects on fMRI brain entropy

summaries.en:
Researchers have long suspected that psychedelics work by increasing the brain's entropy—essentially making neural activity more random and flexible. A new Danish study put this popular theory under the microscope by testing thirteen different ways of measuring brain entropy, using brain imaging data from 28 healthy volunteers who received psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms. The scientists conducted 121 brain scans before and after the drug took effect, then carefully compared how each measurement method related to both the volunteers' reported experiences and measurable changes in their brain activity.

The findings reveal a more complicated picture than the simple "entropy increases" hypothesis suggests. Five different entropy metrics showed consistent increases after psilocybin—including measures of how randomly the brain's spatial patterns shifted and how quickly the brain switched between different activity states. However, eight other metrics showed no significant effect at all, and one showed inconsistent results depending on how the data was processed. Most strikingly, the different measurement methods barely correlated with each other, suggesting they are measuring fundamentally different things rather than all capturing one underlying phenomenon called "brain entropy."

This matters because the entropy theory has become central to how scientists think about how psychedelics work, appearing in dozens of recent studies and grant proposals. What this research demonstrates is that we need to be more careful about which specific measurements we use and more honest about what they actually tell us. The findings align with a growing recognition in psychedelic neuroscience that the brain's response to these compounds is multifaceted—not reducible to a single mechanism. As the field moves toward developing psychedelics as medicines, understanding precisely which brain changes matter most for therapeutic effects remains an urgent open question.
summaries.da:
Forskere har længe anført, at psykedelika virker ved at øge entropien i hjernen—essensen at gøre nervøs aktivitet mere tilfældig og fleksibel. Et nyt dansk studie satte denne populære teori under lup ved at teste tretten forskellige måder at måle hjernens entropi på, ved hjælp af hjernebilleddata fra 28 raske frivillige, der fik psilocybin, det aktive stof i tryllevampyfluer. Forskerne gennemførte 121 hjernescans før og efter stoffet tog effekt, og sammenlignede derefter omhyggeligt, hvordan hver målemetode var relateret til både frivilliges rapporterede oplevelser og målelige ændringer i deres hjernaktivitet.

Fundingene afslører et mere kompliceret billede end den simple hypotese om "entropi stiger" foreslår. Fem forskellige entropimål viste konsistente stigninger efter psilocybin—herunder måleenheder for, hvor tilfældig hjernen geografiske mønstre skiftede, og hvor hurtigt hjernen skiftede mellem forskellige aktivitetstilstande. Imidlertid viste otte andre mål ingen betydningsfuld effekt overhovedet, og en viste inkonsistente resultater afhængigt af, hvordan dataene blev behandlet. Mest bemærkelsesværdigt korrelerede de forskellige måleenheder knap med hinanden, hvilket tyder på, at de måler grundlæggende forskellige ting snarere end alle at fange ét underliggende fænomen kaldet "hjernens entropi."

Dette betyder noget, fordi entropiteorien er blevet central for, hvordan videnskabsmændene tænker på, hvordan psykedelika virker, og fremgår i dusinvis af nyere studier og ansøgninger om tilskud. Hvad denne forskning demonstrerer, er, at vi skal være mere forsigtige med, hvilke specifikke målinger vi bruger, og mere ærlig om, hvad de egentlig fortæller os. Fundingene stemmer overens med en voksende anerkendelse inden for psykedelisk neurovidenskab af, at hjernens reaktion på disse stoffer er mangfoldig—ikke reducerbar til en enkelt mekanisme. Efterhånden som feltet bevæger sig mod at udvikle psykedelika som medicin, forbliver forståelsen af præcis hvilke hjernændringer, der betyder mest for terapeutiske effekter, et presserende åbent spørgsmål.

items.title: Quantifying psilocybin exposure in a natural product–based retreat setting: An observational field method for dose measurement

summaries.en:
When people consume psilocybin mushrooms at retreat centres, nobody really knows how much of the active compound they're actually ingesting. A new study tackled this practical problem by developing a simple field method to measure psilocybin doses in real-world retreat settings, where people gather to explore the potential therapeutic effects of these fungi. Researchers observed participants at natural product–based retreats and created a straightforward way to quantify the actual psilocybin exposure people received, moving beyond guesswork and rough estimates that have long plagued informal psychedelic use.

This observational approach is significant because most psilocybin research happens in controlled laboratory conditions with precisely measured doses, but people seeking healing or insight often turn to retreat centres that operate in less regulated environments. The gap between what happens in the clinic and what happens in the field has made it difficult for researchers to understand real-world outcomes or compare different retreat experiences. By developing practical measurement techniques that work outside the lab, scientists can now begin to gather honest data about what people actually experience and whether variations in dosing correlate with different outcomes.

This work arrives at a crucial moment in psychedelic science. As interest in psilocybin therapy grows and more retreat centres emerge to meet demand, the field faces mounting pressure to understand what happens in these uncontrolled spaces. Regulatory bodies, retreat organisers, and participants themselves need reliable information about dosing and safety. Several parallel initiatives are pushing for better standardisation and transparency in psychedelic retreat settings. This study represents a practical bridge between the rigorous science of clinical trials and the messy reality of how people actually use these medicines, helping ensure that future research can build on solid ground rather than speculation.
summaries.da:
Når mennesker spiser psilocybin-svampe ved retreatcentre, ved næsten ingen præcist, hvor meget af det aktive stof de faktisk får i sig. Et nyt studie tog fat på denne praktiske udfordring ved at udvikle en simpel feltmetode til at måle psilocybin-doser i virkelige retreatmiljøer, hvor mennesker samles for at udforske de potentielle terapeutiske virkninger af disse svampe. Forskere observerede deltagere på naturprodukt-baserede retreats og skabte en ligetil måde at kvantificere den faktiske psilocybin-eksponering, folk fik, væk fra gætværk og grove estimater, som længe har plaget uformel psykedelika-brug.

Denne observationsbaserede tilgang betyder meget, fordi de fleste psilocybin-undersøgelser foregår under kontrollerede laboratoriebetingelser med præcist målt dosering, men mennesker, der søger helbredelse eller indsigt, henvender sig ofte til retreatcentre, som opererer i mindre regulerede omgivelser. Kløften mellem, hvad der sker i klinikken og hvad der sker på feltet, har gjort det vanskeligt for forskere at forstå virkelige resultater eller sammenligne forskellige retreat-oplevelser. Ved at udvikle praktiske måle-teknikker, der virker uden for laboratoriet, kan videnskabsmænd nu begynde at indsamle ærlige data om, hvad mennesker faktisk oplever, og om variationer i dosering korrelerer med forskellige resultater.

Dette arbejde kommer på et afgørende tidspunkt inden for psykedelika-videnskaben. Efterhånden som interessen for psilocybin-terapi vokser, og flere retreatcentre dukker op for at møde efterspørgslen, står området over for stigende pres for at forstå, hvad der sker på disse ukontrollerede steder. Reguleringsmyndigheder, retreatorganisatorer og deltagere selv har brug for pålidelige oplysninger om dosering og sikkerhed. Adskillige parallelle initiativer presser på for bedre standardisering og transparens på psykedelika-retreats. Dette studie repræsenterer en praktisk bro mellem den strenge videnskab fra kliniske forsøg og det rodede virkelighed, hvor mennesker faktisk bruger disse stoffer, hvilket hjælper med at sikre, at fremtidig forskning kan bygge på et solidt grundlag.

items.title: Learnings from a hybrid communities of practice group therapy model to support psilocybin-assisted therapy for patients with a terminal diagnosis.

summaries.en:
When facing a terminal illness, the psychological toll can be as overwhelming as the physical symptoms. A groundbreaking study has explored whether psilocybin-assisted therapy—a treatment combining the psychedelic compound psilocybin with guided psychological support—might help cancer patients find peace and renewed meaning in their final chapters. The research tackled a practical challenge that has limited access to these promising treatments: most studies have focused on one-on-one therapy, which is expensive and time-consuming. Instead, researchers designed a hybrid group model where 25 patients participated in weekly community sessions over six to eight weeks, culminating in a single psilocybin-assisted therapy session conducted together. The community meetings, held virtually, included preparation sessions before the medicine experience and integration sessions afterward, allowing participants to build trust and safety with one another before and after their journey.

The results were striking. Over the course of a year, 31 therapy sessions were delivered across four rotating groups, with an impressive 84% completion rate. Participants reported feeling greater trust in themselves, a notably improved outlook on life, and stronger connections to the people around them. These outcomes emerged from careful qualitative research—the team interviewed participants using open-ended questions and identified recurring themes in their responses, rather than relying solely on numerical scores. The peer support that naturally developed within the group proved essential; witnessing others' experiences and being witnessed in return created a unique healing container.

This finding arrives at a pivotal moment for psychedelic research. Scientists have accumulated compelling evidence that psilocybin can reduce existential distress and death anxiety in terminal cancer patients, but access remains limited and prohibitively expensive for most people. The hybrid community model addresses this bottleneck by combining the relational power of group support with the transformative potential of the medicine itself. It echoes broader trends in psychedelic medicine toward more accessible, scalable approaches—moving beyond the elite, clinic-based model toward formats that harness human connection. The study raises intriguing questions: Could this model work for other conditions? How essential is the group experience to the therapeutic outcome? And as psychedelics move toward medical acceptance, will community-centered approaches like this become the standard?
summaries.da:
At stå overfor en terminal sygdom kan være psykologisk så overvældende som fysisk. Et banebrydende studie har udforsket, om psykedelika-assisteret terapi—en behandling, der kombinerer det psykedeliske stof psilocybin med guidet psykologisk support—kan hjælpe kræftpatienter med at finde fred og fornyet mening i deres sidste kapitel. Forskningen tog fat på en praktisk udfordring, der har begrænset adgangen til disse lovende behandlinger: de fleste studier har fokuseret på en-til-en terapi, som er dyr og tidskrævende. I stedet designede forskerne en hybrid gruppemodel, hvor 25 patienter deltog i ugentlige fællesskabsmøder over seks til otte uger, som kulminerede med en enkelt psykedelika-assisteret terapisession i gruppen. Fællesskabsmøderne, afholdt virtuelt, omfattede forberedelsessessioner før medicinoplevelsen og integrationssessioner efter, hvilket gav deltagerne mulighed for at bygge tillid og sikkerhed med hinanden før og efter deres rejse.

Resultaterne var slående. Over et år blev 31 terapisessioner leveret på tværs af fire roterende grupper, med en imponerende gennemførelsesrate på 84 procent. Deltagerne rapporterede øget selvtillid, væsentligt forbedret livssyn og stærkere forbindelser til mennesker omkring dem. Disse resultater kom fra omhyggelig kvalitativ forskning—holdet interviewede deltagere med åbne spørgsmål og identificerede tilbagevendende temaer i deres svar frem for at stole alene på numeriske scores. Den peer support, der naturligt udvikledes inden for gruppen, viste sig afgørende; at være vidne til andres erfaringer og blive hørt selv skabte en unik helbredende ramme.

Dette fund ankommer på et afgørende tidspunkt for psykedelika-forskningen. Forskere har samlet overbevisende bevis for, at psilocybin kan reducere eksistentiel angst hos terminal kræftpatienter, men adgangen forbliver begrænset og uoverkommelig dyr for de fleste. Hybrid-fællesskabsmodellen løser dette problem ved at kombinere gruppestøttens relationelle kraft med medicinens transformative potentiale. Det gentager bredere tendenser inden for psykedelika-medicin mod mere tilgængelige, skalerbare tilgange—væk fra elitebaserede kliniske modeller hen imod formater, der udnytter menneskelig forbindelse. Studiet rejser interessante spørgsmål: Kunne denne model fungere for andre tilstande? Hvor væsentlig er gruppeoplevelsen for det terapeutiske resultat? Og når psykedelika bevæger sig mod medicinsk accept, vil fællesskabscentrerede tilgange som denne blive standarden?

items.title: Molecules, meaning, and physiology: disentangling the active ingredients of psychedelic therapeutics

summaries.en: Psychedelic-assisted therapy is delivering remarkable results for people struggling with depression, anxiety, and other psychiatric conditions—often producing improvements that last long after a single session. Yet scientists still don't fully understand why. When someone takes a full dose of a psychedelic like psilocybin or LSD, three things happen simultaneously: the drug floods the brain with chemical signals, the person experiences intense, often meaningful visions and emotions, and their body undergoes dramatic physiological shifts—heart racing, breathing changes, and heightened body awareness. This tangle of simultaneous effects makes it nearly impossible to figure out which piece is actually doing the therapeutic work. A new perspective proposes using three complementary research tools to untangle this puzzle. First, giving people a tiny sub-threshold dose of a psychedelic lets researchers study the raw neurochemical effects without the overwhelming experience. Second, intensive breathwork breathing exercises can trigger profound emotional and bodily shifts without any drug involved, isolating the role of the nervous system itself. Third, stimulating the vagus nerve a key nerve running through the body can probe how physical sensations influence mood and thought, again without altered consciousness. By studying these three approaches in parallel, within the same experimental framework, researchers hope to pinpoint whether therapeutic change comes mainly from chemical brain changes, from the meaningful psychological experiences people have, or from shifts in body-based awareness. This methodological clarity comes at a crucial moment, as psychedelic therapy moves from research labs toward clinical reality, making it essential to understand and potentially optimize exactly how these remarkable treatments work.
summaries.da: Psykedelika-assisteret terapi leverer bemærkelsesværdige resultater for mennesker, der kæmper med depression, angst og andre psykiatriske tilstande—ofte med forbedringer, der varer længe efter en enkelt session. Men videnskabsfolk forstår stadig ikke helt hvorfor. Når nogle får en fuld dosis af et psykedelikum som psilocybin eller LSD, sker der tre ting samtidigt: stoffet oversvømmer hjernen med kemiske signaler, personen oplever intense, ofte meningsfulde visioner og følelser, og kroppen gennemgår dramatiske fysiologiske ændringer—hjerte der banker, ændringer i vejrtrækningen og øget kropsbevidsthed. Denne sammenvikling af samtidige effekter gør det næsten umuligt at finde ud af, hvilken del der rent faktisk fremkalder den terapeutiske virkning. Et nyt perspektiv foreslår at bruge tre komplementære forskningsværktøjer til at løse dette puslespil. Først kan man give mennesker en mikroskopisk sub-tærskelværdi dosis af et psykedelikum for at studere de rene neurochemiske effekter uden den overvældende oplevelse. Anden, intensiv vejrtrækningsøvelser kan udløse dybe følelsesmæssige og fysiske skift uden noget stof, hvilket isolerer nervesystemets rolle. Tredje, stimulering af vagusnerven—en nøglenerve, der løber gennem kroppen—kan undersøge, hvordan fysiske fornemmelser påvirker humør og tanker, igen uden ændret bevidsthed. Ved at studere disse tre tilgange parallelt inden for samme eksperimentelle ramme håber forskere at præcisere, om terapeutisk ændring primært stammer fra kemiske hjernefunktioner, fra de meningsfulde psykologiske oplevelser, mennesker har, eller fra skift i kropsbaseret bevidsthed. Denne metodiske klarhed kommer på et afgørende tidspunkt, når psykedelika-terapi bevæger sig fra forskningslaboratorier mod klinisk virkelighed, hvilket gør det væsentligt at forstå og potentielt optimere præcis hvordan disse bemærkelsesværdige behandlinger virker.

items.title: Psychological change processes in alcohol use disorder: A qualitative study of 5‐methoxy‐ N , N ‐dimethyltryptamine (5‐MeO‐DMT) with cognitive behavioural therapy

summaries.en:
Researchers in London have investigated how a single dose of 5-MeO-DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound, might help people overcome alcohol addiction when combined with therapy. Ten people with serious alcohol use disorder participated in the study alongside trained therapists. Over three months, participants received one intranasal dose of the psychedelic alongside cognitive behavioural therapy—a well-established talking therapy focused on preventing relapse—and psychological support. The team conducted detailed interviews with both the participants and their therapists to understand what actually changed in people's minds and behaviour during this time, rather than just measuring outcomes with numbers.

What emerged was a picture of how psychedelics might work differently than traditional treatment approaches. Participants described shifts in how they viewed their drinking, new insights about their motivations, and changes in their sense of self that seemed to complement the structured therapy they received. The therapists confirmed these observations, noting that the combination appeared to create moments of openness and reflection that strengthened the therapeutic work. While this was a small study designed mainly to check safety—not to prove the treatment works—the qualitative findings hint at psychological mechanisms that might explain why some people respond well to psychedelics paired with skilled therapeutic support.

This research sits at an important moment in psychedelic science. The field is moving beyond simply asking "does it work?" to asking "how does it work and for whom?" Understanding the lived experience of participants, not just clinical measurements, is crucial as psychedelics move toward potential medical use. The study also highlights a growing recognition that psychedelics alone are not magic cures; their power may lie in how they open psychological doors that skilled therapists can help people walk through. Questions remain about which individuals benefit most, how crucial the therapy component is, and whether effects persist long-term.
summaries.da:
Forskere i London har undersøgt, hvordan en enkelt dosis 5-MeO-DMT, et kraftigt psykedelikum, kan hjælpe mennesker med at overvinde alkoholafhængighed, når det kombineres med terapi. Ti personer med alvorlig alkoholforgiftning deltog i studiet sammen med uddannede terapeuter. Over tre måneder modtog deltagerne en enkelt næsedosis psykedelikum sammen med kognitiv adfærdsterapi—en velkendt talketerapi fokuseret på tilbagefaldsprevention—og psykologisk støtte. Forskergruppen gennemførte detaljerede interviews med både deltagerne og deres terapeuter for at forstå, hvad der egentlig ændrede sig i menneskers sind og adfærd i denne tid, i stedet for blot at måle resultater med tal.

Det der fremkom, var et billede af, hvordan psykedelika kan virke anderledes end traditionelle behandlingstilgange. Deltagerne beskrev skift i, hvordan de så deres drikken, nye indsigter om deres motivationer, og ændringer i deres selvforståelse, som syntes at supplere den strukturerede terapi, de modtog. Terapeuterne bekræftede disse observationer og bemærkede, at kombinationen syntes at skabe øjeblikke af åbenhed og refleksion, der styrkede det terapeutiske arbejde. Selvom dette var et lille studie designet hovedsageligt til at kontrollere sikkerhed—ikke til at bevise, at behandlingen virker—peger de kvalitative fund på psykologiske mekanismer, der måske kan forklare, hvorfor nogle mennesker reagerer godt på psykedelika kombineret med dygtig terapeutisk støtte.

Denne forskning finder sted på et vigtigt tidspunkt inden for psykedelika-videnskab. Feltet bevæger sig væk fra blot at spørge "virker det?" til at spørge "hvordan virker det, og for hvem?" At forstå deltagernes faktiske oplevelses, ikke kun kliniske målinger, er afgørende, når psykedelika bevæger sig mod potentiel medicinsk brug. Studiet fremhæver også en voksende erkendelse af, at psykedelika ikke er mirakelkure i sig selv; deres kraft kan ligge i, hvordan de åbner psykologiske døre, som dygtige terapeuter kan hjælpe mennesker med at gå gennem. Spørgsmål bliver ved med at eksistere omkring, hvilke personer der har størst gavn, hvor vigtig terapidelen er, og om effekterne varer ved over længere tid.

items.title: Where is the sweet spot for psychedelic-enhanced fear extinction? An integrative quantitative synthesis of dose–effect patterns in rodent models

summaries.en: Scientists have long suspected that psychedelics might help people overcome deep-seated fears, and new research suggests they may have found the optimal doses for making this work. Researchers analyzed data from 177 experiments studying how three psychedelics—DMT, MDMA, and ketamine—helped rodents unlearn fearful responses in laboratory settings. Using advanced statistical techniques, they pooled results across studies and adjusted for differences in how potent each drug is, asking a simple question: does fear extinction improve steadily as doses increase, or is there a sweet spot where too much actually becomes counterproductive? The findings painted an interesting picture. For classical psychedelics like DMT and ketamine, the relationship was surprisingly linear—meaning lower doses generally produced stronger beneficial effects on fear extinction within the range tested, and there was no evidence of a harmful "more is worse" pattern. MDMA showed a different pattern, but the overall picture suggested that when it comes to fear extinction, less might indeed be more. The researchers also found that the timing between giving the drug and testing whether animals had overcome their fear mattered, especially for classical psychedelics. Interestingly, factors like the animal's sex and age didn't seem to shift these patterns. This work arrives at a crucial moment in psychedelic science, as researchers worldwide are racing to translate promising animal findings into human treatments for anxiety disorders and PTSD. Understanding the dose-response relationship—how much drug produces what effect—is foundational before any therapy reaches patients. However, the researchers note important limitations: there wasn't enough data on LSD to draw firm conclusions, and rodent brains don't perfectly mirror human neurobiology, so these findings are best seen as signposts rather than final answers.
summaries.da: Forskere har længe suspekteret, at psykedelika kunne hjælpe mennesker med at overvinde dybt siddende frygt, og ny forskning tyder på, at de måske har fundet de optimale doser til at få det til at fungere. Forskere analyserede data fra 177 eksperimenter, der undersøgte, hvordan tre psykedelika—DMT, MDMA og ketamin—hjalp gnavere med at glemme frygtresponser i laboratoriemiljøer. Ved hjælp af avancerede statistiske teknikker sammenfattede de resultater på tværs af studier og justerede for forskelle i, hvor potent hvert stof er, og stillede et simpelt spørgsmål: forbedres frygtudslettelse konstant, når doserne stiger, eller findes der et sødt punkt, hvor for meget faktisk bliver skadeligt? Resultaterne malede et interessant billede. For klassiske psykedelika som DMT og ketamin var forholdet overraskende lineært—hvilket betyder, at lavere doser generelt producerede stærkere gavnlige effekter på frygtudslettelse inden for det testede område, og der var ingen tegn på et skadeligt "mere er værre" mønster. MDMA viste et anderledes mønster, men det overordnede billede tydede på, at mindre måske virkelig er mere, når det kommer til frygtudslettelse. Forskerne fandt også, at timingen mellem administration af stoffet og test af, hvorvidt dyrene havde overvundet deres frygt, var vigtig, især for klassiske psykedelika. Interessant nok forekom faktorer som dyrets køn og alder ikke at ændre disse mønstre. Dette arbejde kommer på et afgørende tidspunkt inden for psykedelikaforskning, da forskere verden over kappedeles om at oversætte lovende dyreforsøgsfund til humane behandlinger for angstlidelser og PTSD. At forstå dosis-respons-forholdet—hvor meget stof producerer hvilken effekt—er grundlæggende, før nogen terapi når til patienter. Forskerne bemærker dog vigtige begrænsninger: der var ikke nok data om LSD til at drage sikre konklusioner, og gnaverhjerner afspejler ikke perfekt menneskelig neurobiologi, så disse resultater er bedst set som vejvisere snarere end endelige svar.

items.title: Safety and Efficacy of Psilocybin During Anticancer Treatment: A Phase II Trial Secondary Analysis.

summaries.en: Phase II secondary analysis (N=30) examining psilocybin-assisted therapy safety and efficacy in cancer patients with depression. Participants received 25 mg psilocybin with preparation and integration therapy. Depression scores (MADRS) improved substantially in both groups—those receiving concurrent anticancer treatment (n=17) and those not (n=13)—with no significant between-group differences at weeks 1, 3, or 8. Adverse events were frequent but comparable; four severe and one serious adverse event occurred only in the treatment group, though deemed unrelated to psilocybin.
summaries.da: Phase II-analyse (N=30) af sikkerhed og effektivitet ved psykedelika-assisteret terapi hos kræftpatienter med depression. Deltagerne fik 25 mg psykedelika med forberedelse og integrationsbehandling. Depressionsscore (MADRS) forbedres betydeligt i begge grupper—både dem i samtidsbehandling med cancermedicin (n=17) og uden (n=13)—uden signifikante gruppeforskelle ved uge 1, 3 eller 8. Bivirkninger var hyppige men sammenlignelige; fire alvorlige og en alvorlig bivirkning forekom kun i behandlingsgruppen, vurderet som uafhængig af psykedelika.

items.title: Psychological change processes in alcohol use disorder: A qualitative study of 5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine (5-MeO-DMT) with cognitive behavioural therapy.

summaries.en: This qualitative sub-study embedded in a phase 2a open-label trial examined psychological change processes in 10 participants with moderate to severe alcohol use disorder treated with a single intranasal dose of 5-MeO-DMT alongside cognitive behavioural therapy for relapse prevention. Semi-structured interviews with participants (Day 1 and Day 84) and therapists explored acute experiences, perceived behavioural changes, and the role of psychological support over 12 weeks.
summaries.da: Denne kvalitative undersøgelse, indlejret i et fase 2a-forsøg, undersøgte psykologiske forandringsprocesser hos 10 deltagere med moderat til svær alkoholforgiftning behandlet med en enkelt intranasal dosis 5-MeO-DMT sammen med kognitiv adfærdsterapi til tilbagefaldsprevention. Semistrukturerede interviews med deltagere (dag 1 og dag 84) og terapeuter udforsker akutte erfaringer, opfattede adfærdsændringer og støttens rolle over 12 uger.

items.title: Capacity Building Through Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy: Navigating Social Determinants of Health.

summaries.en: This perspective piece critiques neurocentric approaches to psychedelic-assisted therapy (PAT), arguing they overlook experiential and social dimensions crucial to outcomes. The authors propose framing PAT as capacity-building that enhances self-perception and meaningful agency, rather than purely neurobiological intervention. An ecological, relational orientation is essential to address social determinants of health.
summaries.da: Dette perspektivstykke kritiserer neurocentrerede tilgange til psykedelika-assisteret terapi (PAT) for at overse erfaringsmæssige og sociale dimensioner afgørende for resultater. Forfatterne foreslår at ramme PAT som kapacitetsopbygning, der forbedrer selvopfattelse og meningsfuld handlen, frem for rent neurobiologisk intervention. En økologisk, relational tilgang er vigtig for at adressere sociale determinanter for sundhed.

items.title: Ketamine for substance use disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

summaries.en: A meta-analysis of 15 RCTs (798 participants) examined ketamine's efficacy for substance use disorders. Seven trials contributed abstinence data, showing ketamine significantly improved short-term abstinence (<1 month, OR=3.27). However, evidence remains limited and inconclusive regarding long-term efficacy and safety profile, warranting further investigation.
summaries.da: En metaanalyse af 15 RCT'er (798 deltagere) undersøgte ketamins effektivitet for stoffmisbrug. Syv forsøg bidrog med abstinensdata, som viste signifikant forbedret kortvarig abstinens (<1 måned, OR=3,27). Beviserne er dog begrænsede og ikke helt afgørende vedr. langtidseffektivitet og sikkerhedsprofil, hvilket kræver yderligere forskning.

items.title: A Nature-Themed Video Intervention Increases Nature Relatedness in Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy for Alcohol Use Disorder.

summaries.en: This randomized controlled study (N=20) examined whether a nature-themed video intervention enhanced nature relatedness during psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy for alcohol use disorder. Participants viewing a 42-minute nature video showed significantly greater increases in nature relatedness compared to controls, while social connectedness was unaffected. Results suggest nature-themed interventions may selectively potentiate nature relatedness during psychedelic therapy, warranting further investigation of nature immersion and connectedness as therapeutic targets.
summaries.da: Dette randomiseret kontrolstudie (N=20) undersøgte, om en naturtematisk videointerention forbedrede naturrelatedness under psilocybin-assisteret psykoterapy for alkoholforgiftning. Deltagere, der så en 42-minutters naturvideo, viste signifikant større stigning i naturrelatedness sammenlignet med kontroller, mens social forbundethed var uændret. Resultaterne tyder på, at naturtematiske interventioner kan potensiere naturrelatedness under psykedelika-terapi og kræver videre udforskning af naturimersion og forbundethed som terapeutiske mål.

items.title: Psilocybin for Fear of Cancer Recurrence.

summaries.en: A study examining psilocybin's therapeutic potential for cancer patients experiencing fear of recurrence. While limited abstract details are available, the research contributes to emerging clinical evidence exploring psychedelics as adjunctive treatments for anxiety-related psychological distress in oncology settings.
summaries.da: En undersøgelse af psiloxybin's terapeutiske potentiale for kræftpatienter med angst for tilbagefald. Selvom abstrakt-detaljer er begrænsede, bidrager forskningen til voksende klinisk evidens for psykedelika som supplerende behandling af angstrelateret psykologisk belastning inden for onkologi.

items.title: Therapeutic Potential of Psilocybin in Psychiatric Disorders: Mechanisms, Efficacy, and Clinical Implications.

summaries.en: This review examines psilocybin's clinical potential across psychiatric disorders. Early-phase trials show rapid but variable reductions in depressive symptoms, with sustained effects in some cases. Preliminary evidence supports benefits for anxiety in life-threatening illness, substance use disorders, and possible effects in OCD, body dysmorphic disorder, anorexia nervosa, and PTSD. Adverse events are typically mild and transient. Mechanistically, psilocybin may enhance emotional and cognitive flexibility via limbic-prefrontal modulation and synaptic plasticity, particularly with psychotherapeutic support. However, evidence remains limited by small samples and short follow-up; larger rigorous trials are needed.
summaries.da: Dette review undersøger psykedelika-psilocybins kliniske potentiale på tværs af psykiatriske lidelser. Tidlige forsøg viser hurtige men variable reduktioner i depressive symptomer, med vedvarende effekter i nogle tilfælde. Præliminær evidens støtter fordele ved angst ved livstruende sygdom, misbrug og mulige effekter ved OCD, body dysmorphic disorder, anorexia nervosa og PTSD. Bivirkninger er typisk milde og forbigående. Mekanistisk kan psilocybin øge følelsesmæssig og kognitiv fleksibilitet via limbisk-præfrontal modulation og synaptisk plastisitet, især med psykoterapeutisk støtte. Dog er evidensen begrænset af små stikprøver og kort opfølgning; større strenge forsøg er nødvendige.

items.title: Effect of Esketamine on Depressive Symptoms in Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder at Imminent Suicide Risk: A Randomized Psychoactive-Controlled Study.

summaries.en: A phase 2b double-blind RCT (n=147, ages 12-17) compared esketamine nasal spray (56, 84 mg) vs. active control (midazolam) twice weekly for 4 weeks in adolescents with major depression and imminent suicide risk. All received standard care including hospitalization, antidepressants, and psychotherapy. Pooled esketamine doses showed superiority over midazolam on CDRS-R scores at 24 hours post-dose (LS mean difference: -5.8, 95% CI: -11.19 to -0.35). Esketamine rapidly improved depressive symptoms in this high-risk population.
summaries.da: Et fase 2b dobbeltblindet RCT (n=147, alderen 12-17) sammenlignede esketamin-næsespray (56, 84 mg) med aktivt kontrolstof (midazolam) to gange ugentligt i 4 uger hos unge med depression og øjeblikkelig selvmordsrisiko. Alle modtog standardbehandling inklusiv indlæggelse, antidepressiva og psykoterapia. Poolede esketamin-doser viste overlegenhed over midazolam på CDRS-R ved 24 timer efter første dosis (forskel: -5,8, 95% CI: -11,19 til -0,35). Esketamin forbedrede hurtigt depressive symptomer i denne højrisikogruppe.

items.title: Cardiovascular safety of psilocybin in psychiatric practice: a narrative review.

summaries.en: Narrative review examining cardiovascular safety of psilocybin in psychiatric settings. Analysis of clinical trials and pharmacology literature shows supervised psilocybin produces mean systolic/diastolic blood pressure increases of ~19/8.7 mmHg, peaking 60-90 min post-dose and resolving within 4-6 hours. Serious acute cardiovascular events remain rare in screened participants. Risk stratification framework needed as psilocybin-assisted interventions transition from controlled trials to routine psychiatric practice, considering comorbidities and drug interactions.
summaries.da: Narrativ review af kardiovaskulær sikkerhed ved psykedelika i psykiatrisk praksis. Analyse af kliniske forsøg og farmakologi viser, at psykedelika under overvågning medfører gennemsnitlige blodtryksforhøjelser på ~19/8,7 mmHg systolisk/diastolisk, med maksimum 60-90 min efter dosering og normalisering inden for 4-6 timer. Alvorlige akutte kardiovaskulære hændelser er sjældne hos screenede deltagere. Risikostratificering nødvendig ved overgang fra kontrollerede forsøg til rutinebehandling, under hensyn til komorbiditeter og medicin-interaktioner.

items.title: Safety, feasibility, and preliminary clinical outcomes of psilocybin-assisted therapy for veterans with severe, treatment-resistant PTSD: an open-label pilot clinical trial.

summaries.en: Open-label pilot trial evaluating psilocybin-assisted therapy (PAT) for 12 U.S. military veterans with severe, treatment-resistant PTSD. Participants received two psilocybin sessions (15mg and 25mg) with approximately 16 hours of therapy over 2-3 weeks. Primary outcomes assessed safety and suicidal ideation; secondary outcomes measured PTSD symptom severity. Study conducted at Center for Psychedelic Drug Research and Education, Columbus, OH.
summaries.da: Åben pilot-studie af psykedelika-assisteret terapi (PAT) hos 12 amerikanske militærveteraner med alvorlig, behandlingsresistent PTSD. Deltagerne modtog to psykedelika-sessioner (15mg og 25mg) med ca. 16 timers terapi over 2-3 uger. Primære endepunkter målte sikkerhed og selvmordstanker; sekundære endepunkter målte PTSD-symptomers sværhedsgrad. Studiet gennemført på Center for Psychedelic Drug Research and Education i Columbus, OH.

items.title: A retrospective report of a ketamine-augmented, transdiagnostic psychiatric outpatient psychotherapy program.

summaries.en: Retrospective chart review (N=56) of a Canadian outpatient program combining sublingual ketamine with transdiagnostic psychotherapy for Veterans with comorbid depression, anxiety, and PTSD. Four standardized measures showed significant symptom reductions and improved quality of life post-treatment, particularly in moderate-to-severe cases. Results suggest ketamine may enhance neuroplasticity while intensive therapy increases engagement and resilience, though lack of control group limits conclusions.
summaries.da: Retrospektiv journalgennemgang (N=56) af et canadisk ambulant program, der kombinerer sublingual ketamin med tværdiagnostisk psykoterapi for veteraner med komorbid depression, angst og PTSD. Fire standardiserede målinger viste signifikant symptomreduktion og forbedret livskvalitet efter behandling, især ved moderat-svær symptomatik. Resultaterne tyder på, at ketamin kan øge neuroplasticitet, mens intensiv terapi øger engagement og resiliens, selvom mangel på kontrolgruppe begrænser konklusionerne.

items.title: Toward a definition of treatment-resistant posttraumatic stress disorder: A systematic review.

summaries.en: This systematic review of 55 studies examines definitions of treatment-resistant PTSD (TR-PTSD). Researchers found substantial variation in how TR-PTSD is defined across studies investigating pharmacological (n=19), psychosocial (n=16), psychedelic-assisted (n=7), and emerging treatments (n=13). Results were mixed, with some interventions reducing symptoms significantly while others showed limited efficacy. The authors propose standardized criteria considering adherence, treatment delivery, comorbidities, and mechanisms of action to improve clinical decision-making.
summaries.da: Denne systematiske oversigt over 55 studier undersøger defini­tioner af behandlingsresistent PTSD (TR-PTSD). Forskerne fandt betydelig variation i, hvordan TR-PTSD defineres på tværs af studier, der undersøgte farmakologiske (n=19), psykosociale (n=16), psykedelika-assisterede (n=7) og nye behandlinger (n=13). Resultaterne var blandede – nogle interventioner reducerede symptomer betydeligt, mens andre viste begrænset effekt. Forfatterne foreslår standardiserede kriterier, der tager hensyn til compliance, behandlingsudførelse, komorbiditeter og virkningsmekanismer.

items.title: Psychedelics for military and Veteran communities? Research, practice, and policy considerations.

summaries.en: This article examines the therapeutic potential of psychedelics for military personnel and veterans, addressing research evidence, clinical applications, and policy frameworks. The authors consider both the promise of psychedelics in treating trauma-related conditions and the unique considerations required for military populations.
summaries.da: Artiklen undersøger psykedelikas terapeutiske potentiale for militært personel og veteraner, med fokus på forskningsresultater, klinisk praksis og politiske rammer. Forfatterne vurderer både mulighederne for psykedelika i behandling af traumarelaterede tilstande og særlige hensyn for militære populationer.

items.title: Peer support and psychedelics.

summaries.en: This article examines peer support's role in medically and non-medically supervised psychedelic administration. The authors review existing peer-support frameworks from psychedelic and Veteran communities, comparing core competencies to identify synergies and training gaps. As psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy and state services expand, trained facilitators are essential. The work clarifies psychedelic peership—when experienced individuals facilitate others' sessions—and highlights further needs in training and supervision.
summaries.da: Artiklen undersøger peer supports rolle i medicinskt og ikke-medicinskt superviseret psykedelika-administration. Forfatterne gennemgår eksisterende peer-support-frameworks fra psykedelika- og veterancommunities og sammenligner kernekompetencer for at identificere synergier og træningsgab. Efterhånden som psykedelika-assisteret psykoterapi og statslige services ekspanderer, er uddannede facilitatorer væsentlige. Arbejdet præciserer psykedelika-peership – når erfarne personer faciliterer andres sessioner – og fremhæver yderligere behov indenfor træning og supervision.

items.title: Sex-dependent effects of psychedelics: review of evidence from rodent models.

summaries.en: This rodent model review examines sex-dependent effects of psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD, DMT, mescaline, and related compounds) acting via 5-HT2A receptor agonism. Evidence reveals notable sex differences in pharmacodynamics, serotonergic and dopaminergic signaling, amygdala reactivity, and dendritic spine formation. Behavioral outcomes—head twitch responses, locomotor activity, prepulse inhibition, stress reactivity, and social behavior—frequently show stronger or distinct effects in females, with ovarian cycle phase further modulating responses. Disease models demonstrate sex-dependent therapeutic outcomes for alcohol consumption and affective behavior. The review concludes sex is a critical biological variable in psychedelic neurobiology and behavioral effects.
summaries.da: Dette rodent-modelreview undersøger kønsafhængige effekter af psykedelika (psilocybin, LSD, DMT, meskalin og relaterede stoffer) som virker via 5-HT2A-receptoragonisme. Evidensen viser betydelige kønsforskelle i farmakodynamik, serotonergt og dopaminergt signalering, amygdalarespons og dendrittiske ryg-dannelse. Adfærdsmæssige resultater—head twitch-respons, motorisk aktivitet, prepulse-inhibition, stressreaktivitet og social adfærd—viser ofte stærkere eller forskellige effekter hos hunner, hvor ovariefasecyklus yderligere modulerer responserne. Sygdomsmodeller demonstrerer kønsafhængige terapeutiske udfald for alkoholforbrug og affektiv adfærd. Reviewet konkluderer, at køn er en kritisk biologisk variabel i psykedelikas neurobiologi og adfærdsmæssige effekter.

items.title: Treatment-resistant Depression in the Post-ketamine Era: Unmet Needs beyond Rapid Response.

summaries.en: Ketamine and esketamine have revolutionized treatment-resistant depression (TRD) by inducing rapid antidepressant effects within hours. However, critical questions remain: durability of initial benefits, relapse prevention, maintenance and tapering strategies, functional recovery outcomes, patient selection criteria, predictive biomarkers, and long-term safety of repeated glutamatergic treatment. This review argues that research priorities should shift from acute efficacy to durability, functional recovery, and implementation value.
summaries.da: Ketamin og esketamin har transformeret behandlingen af depressiv lidelse, der modstår medicinsk behandling (TRD) ved at inducere hurtig antidepressiv effekt inden for timer. Kritiske spørgsmål forbliver ubesvarede: varighed af initial effekt, tilbagefaldsprophylakse, vedligeholdelses- og nedtrapningsstrategier, funktionel bedring, patientudvælgelse, prædiktive biomarkører og langtidssikkerhed ved gentaget glutamatergi. Reviewet argumenterer for, at forskningsprioriteter bør skiftes fra akut effektivitet til varighed, funktionel bedring og implementeringsværdi.

items.title: Politically Salient Events May Modulate Effects of Naturalistic Psychedelic Use on Support for Partisan Violence.

summaries.en: A longitudinal observational study (n=12,345 at follow-up) examined how timing of naturalistic psychedelic use relates to support for partisan violence. Among 505 participants reporting psychedelic use over two months, those whose most intense experience occurred on July 4th (n=19) showed decreased support for partisan violence. Similar associations appeared for experiences timed with the Trump assassination attempt. Conversely, psychedelic experiences near party conventions or Election Day were associated with increased support for partisan violence. Results suggest sociocultural context modulates psychedelics' effects on political attitudes.
summaries.da: Et længdeforløbsstudie (n=12.345 ved opfølgning) undersøgte sammenhængen mellem timing af naturalistisk psykedelika-brug og støtte til partidan vold. Blandt 505 deltagere, der rapporterede psykedelika-brug over to måneder, viste de med mest intens oplevelse på juli 4. (n=19) reduceret støtte til partisan vold. Lignende sammenhænge fandtes for oplevelser tidssat med mordattentat på Trump. Omvendt var psykedelika-oplevelser nær partikongresser eller valgdagen forbundet med øget støtte til partisan vold. Resultaterne tyder på, at sociokulturel kontekst modulerer psykedelikas effekter på politiske holdninger.

items.title: Convergent neuroimmune signaling underlying rapid antidepressant response to ketamine and psychedelics.

summaries.en: Researchers integrated CSF proteomics, iPSC transcriptomics, MEG, and plasma cytokine analyses to identify shared mechanisms underlying rapid antidepressant response to ketamine and psychedelics. Across multiple modalities (n=16-39 TRD participants, n=11-25 healthy controls), immune signaling molecules IL-15 and MCP-1 emerged as key regulatory hubs. Ketamine responders showed decreased IL-15 and elevated B-cell signaling at baseline, reversed post-treatment. Plasma IL-7 correlated with MEG gamma power across participants, suggesting neuroimmune convergence despite distinct receptor mechanisms.
summaries.da: Forskere integrerede CSF-proteomik, iPSC-transkriptomik, MEG og plasmaprøver for at identificere fælles mekanismer bag hurtig antidepressiv effekt af ketamin og psykedelika. På tværs af flere målemetoder (n=16-39 behandlingsresistente depression-patienter, n=11-25 kontroller) fremstod IL-15 og MCP-1 som vigtige regulatoriske knudepunkter. Ketaminrespondere viste lavere IL-15 og forhøjet B-celle-signalering ved baseline, som blev reverseret efter behandling. Plasma IL-7 korrelerede med MEG-gammaaktivitet, hvilket tyder på neuroimmun konvergens på trods af forskellige receptormekanismer.

items.title: Feasibility, safety and preliminary effects of ibogaine in patients with moderate and severe alcohol use disorder: a pilot, open-label study.

summaries.en: This open-label pilot study examined ibogaine's feasibility and safety in nine patients with moderate to severe alcohol use disorder. Participants received escalating oral doses (20–400 mg) with 24–48 hour hospitalization and continuous monitoring. Primary outcomes assessed cardiovascular effects, vital signs, and adverse effects. QTc interval alterations occurred in five patients, and mild-to-moderate effects (drowsiness, nausea, anxiety) were common at higher doses. Two patients required medication for agitation and hypertension. Most reported reduced alcohol use, though only five completed the study. Results indicate ibogaine's cardiotoxic potential requires rigorous cardiovascular screening.
summaries.da: Dette åbent pilot-studie undersøgte ibogains mulighed og sikkerhed hos ni patienter med moderat til svær alkoholbrug. Deltagere modtog eskalerende orale doser (20–400 mg) med 24–48 timers hospitalisering og kontinuerlig overvågning. Primære udfald vurderede kardiovaskulære effekter, vitale tegn og bivirkninger. QTc-interval-ændringer forekom hos fem patienter, og milde-til-moderate effekter (døsighed, kvalme, angst) var hyppige ved højere doser. To patienter krævede medicin for agitation og hypertension. De fleste rapporterede reduceret alkoholforbrug, selvom kun fem gennemførte studiet. Resultaterne indikerer ibogains kardiotoxiske potentiale kræver stringent kardiovaskulær screening.

items.title: Candidate Biomarkers of Bipolar Disorder Progression: Implications for Ketamine and Psychedelic Interventions.

summaries.en: A narrative review examined biomarkers of bipolar disorder progression and their relevance to ketamine and psychedelic interventions. Synthesizing evidence from PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science searches (December 2025–February 2026), researchers identified associations between advanced bipolar disorder and abnormalities in inflammatory signaling, neurotrophic regulation, neuroimaging, and epigenetic processes. However, findings were heterogeneous with modest effect sizes, predominantly cross-sectional designs, and candidate biomarkers often reflecting current mood state rather than cumulative illness progression. Peripheral BDNF and inflammatory markers showed limited specificity for disease progression.
summaries.da: Et narrativt review undersøgte biomarkører for progressionen af bipolær lidelse og deres relevans for ketamin- og psykedelika-interventioner. Gennem søgninger i PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus og Web of Science (december 2025–februar 2026) identificerede forskerne sammenhænge mellem fremskreden bipolær lidelse og abnormiteter i inflammatorisk signalering, neutrofisk regulering, neuroimaging og epigenetiske processer. Resultaterne var imidlertid heterogene med beskedne effektstørrelser, overvejende tværsnitsdesign, og kandidatbiomarkører afspejlede ofte nuværende humørtilstand snarere end kumulativ sygdomsprogresssion. Periferisk BDNF og inflammatoriske markører viste begrænset specificitet for sygdomsprogresssion.

items.title: Dimensional effect profiles in treatment-resistant depression: A naturalistic, prospective head-to-head comparison of arTMS, esketamine nasal spray, and oral brexpiprazole.

summaries.en: A prospective, naturalistic study compared three treatments for treatment-resistant depression (n=101): esketamine nasal spray, accelerated repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, and brexpiprazole augmentation. After one month, all treatments significantly reduced depressive severity and anhedonia. Brexpiprazole showed greater improvement in rumination, while esketamine enhanced affective and cognitive symptoms. Both esketamine and arTMS demonstrated anxiolytic effects, suggesting distinct dimensional profiles across treatments in routine clinical practice.
summaries.da: En prospektiv, naturalistisk undersøgelse sammenlignede tre behandlinger for behandlingsresistent depression (n=101): esketamin næsespray, accelereret repetitiv transkraniel magnetstimulation og brexpiprazol-augmentering. Efter en måned reducerede alle behandlinger signifikant depressionsalvorsgrad og anhedoni. Brexpiprazol viste større forbedring i rumination, mens psykedelika forbedrede affektive og kognitive symptomer. Både psykedelika og arTMS demonstrerede anxiolytiske effekter med tilsyneladende adskilte dimensionelle profiler.

items.title: Adjunctive Pharmacotherapy for Major Depressive Disorder with Anxiety Symptoms: from Monoamines to Recent Clinical Evidence.

summaries.en: This review examines adjunctive pharmacotherapy for major depressive disorder (MDD) with comorbid anxiety symptoms, which indicate greater severity and poorer outcomes. Focusing on monoamine dysregulation (noradrenaline, serotonin, dopamine), the authors survey clinical evidence for first- and second-line treatments including atypical antipsychotics, bupropion, ketamine/esketamine, lithium, and others. Current guidelines lack specific recommendations for this patient population despite their significant treatment burden.
summaries.da: Denne oversigt undersøger adjuvant farmakologi til depressiv sygdom med samtidig angst, som indikerer større alvor og dårligere udfald. Med fokus på monoamin-dysregulering (noradrenalin, serotonin, dopamin) gennemgår forfatterne kliniske resultater for først- og andenlinjebehandlinger, herunder atypiske antipsykotika, bupropion, ketamin/esketamin og litium. Nuværende retningslinjer mangler specifikke anbefalinger for denne patientgruppe trods deres betydeligt behandlingsbehov.

items.title: Hepatic Safety of Ketamine and Esketamine for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Real-World Cohort Study.

summaries.en: A historical cohort study of 51 patients with treatment-resistant depression receiving IV ketamine or intranasal esketamine at Mayo Clinic (2017-2024) found no clinically meaningful changes in liver enzyme trajectories. Three patients (5.9%) showed elevations ≥2× upper limit of normal, all attributable to alcohol, myalgia, or pre-existing steatosis rather than ketamine or esketamine exposure. Results suggest subanesthetic ketamine and FDA-approved esketamine doses do not pose hepatic safety concerns during therapeutic use.
summaries.da: Et historisk kohortestudie af 51 patienter med behandlingsresistent depression, der modtog IV ketamin eller intranasal esketamin på Mayo Clinic (2017-2024), viste ingen klinisk betydningsfulde ændringer i leverenzymer. Tre patienter (5,9%) havde forhøjelser ≥2× normal øvre grænse, alle tilskrevet alkohol, myalgi eller eksisterende steatose snarere end ketamin eller esketamin. Resultaterne tyder på, at subanæstetiske doser psykedelika ikke udgør hepatisk sikkerhedsrisiko ved terapeutisk brug.

items.title: CB1R-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis may contribute to the antidepressant effects of esketamine in a chronic variable stress male mouse model.

summaries.en: A mouse study examining esketamine's antidepressant mechanisms found that CB1 cannabinoid receptor signaling in the hippocampus promotes mitochondrial biogenesis—the creation of new mitochondria. Chronically stressed mice treated with a single esketamine dose showed normalized mitochondrial markers (NRF1, TFAM, cytochrome c) and reversed depressive-like behaviors. Blocking CB1 receptors with antagonists prevented both effects, indicating CB1R signaling is essential for esketamine's rapid antidepressant action.
summaries.da: Et musestudium undersøgte esketamins antidepressive mekanismer og fandt, at CB1-cannabinoidreceptorsignalering i hippocampus fremmer mitokondriebiogerese—dannelsen af nye mitokondrier. Kronisk stressede mus behandlet med en enkelt esketamindosis viste normaliserede mitokondriemarører (NRF1, TFAM, cytokrom c) og reverserede depressionslignende adfærd. Blokering af CB1-receptorer med antagonister forhindrede begge effekter, hvilket indikerer, at CB1R-signalering er væsentlig for esketamins hurtige antidepressive virkning.

items.title: Systems-based psychiatry: insights from psychedelic research on mechanisms of healing.

summaries.en: This theoretical paper proposes a systems-based framework for psychiatry, arguing that mental disorders reflect stable patterns within dynamic multilevel systems rather than isolated biological dysfunction. Drawing on neuroscience, complexity science, and psychedelic research, the authors conceptualize therapeutic change as a three-phase process: perturbation, reorganization, and consolidation. Psychedelics exemplify this mechanism by transiently destabilizing entrenched patterns, increasing flexibility for reorganization. Recovery is reframed as enhanced coherence and adaptive capacity across domains, not merely symptom reduction. This model generalizes across therapeutic modalities and has implications for clinical practice and research design.
summaries.da: Dette teoretiske paper foreslår en systembaseret ramme for psykiatri, idet forfatterne argumenterer, at psykiske lidelser afspejler stabile mønstre inden for dynamiske flerniveausystemer snarere end isoleret biologisk dysfunktion. Med udgangspunkt i neurovidenskab, kompleksitetsforskning og psykedelika-forskning konceptualiserer de terapeutisk forandring som en trefaset proces: perturbation, reorganisering og konsolidering. Psykedelika eksemplificerer denne mekanisme ved at destabilisere indgroede mønstre midlertidigt, hvilket øger fleksibilitet til reorganisering. Helbredelse omrammes som øget sammenhæng og adaptiv kapacitet på tværs af funktionelle domæner, ikke blot symptomreduktion. Modellen generaliserer på tværs af terapeutiske modaliteter og har implikationer for klinisk praksis og forskningsdesign.

items.title: Esketamine in Treatment-Resistant Depression: Clinical and Translational Perspectives.

summaries.en: This mini-review synthesizes clinical and translational evidence on intranasal esketamine for treatment-resistant depression. The NMDA receptor antagonist produces rapid antidepressant effects within hours by enhancing glutamatergic signaling and activating the AMPA-BDNF-mTOR pathway involved in synaptic plasticity. Randomized controlled trials show consistent reductions in depressive symptoms, though suicidality effects varied. Common adverse events—transient dissociation, dizziness, modest blood pressure increases—are generally self-limiting. Evidence supports esketamine as an effective rapid-acting intervention for treatment-resistant cases.
summaries.da: Denne oversigtsartikel opsummerer kliniske og translationelle studier af intranasal esketamin til behandlingsresistent depression. NMDA-receptorantagonisten frembringer hurtige antidepressive effekter inden for timer ved at øge glutamaterg signalering og aktivere AMPA-BDNF-mTOR-signalvejen involveret i synaptisk plastisitet. Randomiserede kontrollerede forsøg viser konsistente reduktioner i depressive symptomer, selvom effekter på suicidalitet varierede. Almindelige bivirkninger—forbigående disassociation, svimmelhed, beskeden blodtryksstigning—er typisk forbigående. Evidensen støtter esketamin som en effektiv hurtigtvirkende behandling for behandlingsresistent depression.

items.title: [Illicit use of classic psychedelics and suicidality: A systematic literature review].

summaries.en: This systematic review examined the relationship between illicit use of classic psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD, DMT, mescaline) and suicidality outcomes. Following PRISMA guidelines, researchers searched PubMed-Medline and Scopus databases through March 2026 using targeted keyword sequences. The review aimed to clarify mixed findings in existing literature regarding effects on suicidal ideation, planning, attempts, and completed suicides.
summaries.da: Dette systematiske review undersøgte sammenhængen mellem ulovlig brug af psykedelika (psilocybin, LSD, DMT, meskalin) og selvmordsforsøg. Forskerne søgte efter studier i PubMed-Medline og Scopus-databaser til marts 2026 efter PRISMA-retningslinjerne med strukturerede søgeord. Reviewet søgte at præcisere modstridende resultater i eksisterende litteratur angående påvirkning af selvmordstanker, -planlægning, -forsøg og fuldbyrdede selvmord.

items.title: Reply to "Reading the Signal: What Psychedelic Trials in Depression Still Can't Tell Us".

summaries.en: This reply addresses methodological critiques of psychedelic depression trials. Without access to the full abstract, the response likely defends trial design choices and discusses what current evidence can and cannot establish regarding psychedelics' efficacy in treating depression.
summaries.da: Dette svar behandler metodologiske kritikpunkter af psykedelika-forsøg ved depression. Uden adgang til det fulde abstract forsvarer svaret sandsynligvis valg af forsøgsdesign og diskuterer, hvad nuværende evidens kan og ikke kan fastslå om psykedelikas effektivitet ved depression.

items.title: Q1 2026: Oregon Psilocybin Services Update

summaries.en: Oregon Psilocybin Services released its first Q1 2026 dataset, covering January–March. The report provides data on product sales, client demographics and motivations, safety metrics, and key stakeholders in Oregon's regulated psilocybin services infrastructure. The comprehensive tracker offers insights into the state's operational framework for supervised psilocybin-assisted services.
summaries.da: Oregon Psilocybin Services offentliggjorde sit første datasæt for Q1 2026, der dækker januar–marts. Rapporten indeholder data om produktsalg, klientdemografi og motivationer, sikkerhedsmålinger og vigtige aktører i Oregons infrastruktur for regulerede psykedelika-assisterede tjenester. Trackeren giver indsigt i statens operationelle rammeværk.

items.title: Quality of life and productivity among esketamine responders in a real-world study in Australia and New Zealand.

summaries.en: A 16-week real-world study from Australia and New Zealand examined esketamine nasal spray combined with oral antidepressants in 84 treatment-resistant depression patients. Among 28 responders (33.3%), the analysis found mean improvements of 71.2% in depression severity, 29.5% in quality of life (AQoL-8D), and 11.9% or greater in work productivity (WPAI:SHP). Mental health showed the largest quality-of-life gain (32.9%), while work productivity loss improved most (35.9%).
summaries.da: Et 16-ugers real-world studie fra Australien og New Zealand undersøgte esketamin næsespray kombineret med oral antidepressiva hos 84 patienter med behandlingsresistent depression. Blandt 28 respondenters (33,3%) fandt analysen gennemsnitlige forbedringer på 71,2% i depressionsalvor, 29,5% i livskvalitet (AQoL-8D) og 11,9% eller større i arbejdsproduktivitet (WPAI:SHP). Mental sundhed viste størst livskvalitetsgevinst (32,9%), mens arbejdsproduktivitetstab forbedrades mest (35,9%).

items.title: Time-dependent effects of rapid-acting antidepressants in iPSC-derived neurons from treatment-resistant depression and healthy volunteers.

summaries.en: This study used iPSC-derived cortical neurons from treatment-resistant depression patients and healthy controls to investigate rapid-acting antidepressants including ketamine metabolite HNK, psilocybin, LSD, and DOI. After 6 and 24 hours of exposure, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that despite different pharmacological targets, all compounds showed highly correlated gene expression patterns, converging on inflammation, mTORC1 signaling, and cellular growth pathways. HNK demonstrated distinct cell-type-specific effects in excitatory neurons. Results were validated against CSF proteomics from ketamine-treated individuals.
summaries.da: Studiet anvendte iPSC-afledt kortikale neuroner fra patienter med behandlingsresistent depression og raske kontroller til at undersøge hurtigtvirkende antidepressiva inklusiv ketamin-metabolit HNK, psilocybin, LSD og DOI. Efter 6 og 24 timers eksponering viste bulk og single-cell RNA-sekvensering, at alle stoffer på trods af forskellige farmakologiske måls havde højt korreleret genekspression, konvergerende på inflammations-, mTORC1-signalerings- og cellulær vækst-veje. HNK demonstrerede distinkte celletypespeficifikke effekter i excitatoric neuroner. Resultater blev valideret mod cerebrospinalvæske-proteomik fra ketamin-behandlede individer.

items.title: MDMA as an early post-trauma intervention in a translational animal model of PTSD.

summaries.en: A controlled rat study (N=175) examined MDMA's potential to prevent PTSD when administered early after trauma. Predator scent stress-exposed rats received MDMA (2.5–10 mg/kg) or saline at 30 minutes or 24 hours post-trauma. The 10 mg/kg dose significantly reduced anxiety, startle response, and contextual fear when given early or delayed with cue pairing. This dose increased corticosterone, hippocampal glucocorticoid receptors, and markers of neuroplasticity (c-Fos, TPH2, oxytocin). Results suggest psychedelics may prevent chronic PTSD development through neurobiological mechanisms.
summaries.da: Et kontrolleret rattestudie (N=175) undersøgte psykedelikas potentiale til at forebygge PTSD når det gives tidligt efter trauma. Rotter eksponeret for rovdyr-lugtstress fik MDMA (2,5–10 mg/kg) eller saltvandsløsning 30 minutter eller 24 timer efter trauma. Dosen på 10 mg/kg reducerede signifikant angst, startle-respons og kontekstuel frygt når det blev givet tidligt eller forsinket med signal-parring. Denne dosis øgede corticosteron, hippokampale glukokortikoid-receptorer og neuroplasticitetsmærkører (c-Fos, TPH2, oxytocin). Resultaterne tyder på, at psykedelika kan forebygge kronisk PTSD gennem neurobiologiske mekanismer.

items.title: Targeting TLR4/PPARα-mediated neuroinflammation in the prefrontal cortex: S-ketamine and S-HNK rapidly alleviate depression-like behaviors.

summaries.en: This preclinical study investigated how S-ketamine and S-hydroxynorketamine (S-HNK) reduce depression-like behaviors in mice exposed to chronic social stress. Male C57BL/6J mice underwent chronic social defeat stress followed by drug treatment, with behavioral testing (sucrose preference, forced swim, social interaction) and neurochemical analysis. Both compounds rapidly reversed stress-induced depression-like behaviors and restored dopamine, serotonin, and norepinephrine levels in the prefrontal cortex. The mechanisms involved suppression of TLR4-mediated neuroinflammation and increased PPARα signaling, reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α). Viral overexpression of TLR4 blocked these therapeutic effects, confirming TLR4 as a critical target.
summaries.da: Dette dyreforsøg undersøgte, hvordan S-ketamin og S-hydroxynorketamin (S-HNK) reducerer depressionsagtige adfærdsmønstre hos mus udsatte for kronisk social stress. Mandlige C57BL/6J-mus blev underkastet kronisk social nederlagsstress efterfulgt af medicinalbehandling med adfærdstestning og neurochemisk analyse. Begge stoffer vendte hurtigt stress-inducerede depressionsagtige symptomer og gendannede dopamin-, serotonin- og noradrenalin-niveauer i præfrontal cortex. Mekanismerne omfattede suppression af TLR4-medieret neuroinflammation og øget PPARα-signalering, hvilket reducerede pro-inflammatoriske cytokiner. Viral overexpression af TLR4 blokerede disse terapeutiske effekter og bekræftede TLR4 som kritisk target.

items.title: Real-World Effectiveness and Cost-Differential of Intranasal Esketamine Versus Intramuscular Ketamine.

summaries.en: A retrospective study of 179 Veterans with treatment-resistant depression compared intramuscular (IM) ketamine to intranasal (IN) esketamine across eight treatments. IM ketamine showed non-inferiority to IN esketamine for depression (PHQ-9 difference: 0.04 points) and PTSD symptoms, with comparable adverse events and hospitalizations. Notably, IM ketamine cost $647 per treatment course versus $6,069 for IN esketamine, suggesting it may be a cost-effective alternative expanding access to ketamine treatment.
summaries.da: Et retrospektivt studie af 179 veteraner med behandlingsresistent depression sammenlignede intramuskulær (IM) ketamin med intranasal (IN) esketamin over otte behandlinger. IM ketamin var ikke-inferior til IN esketamin for depression (PHQ-9-forskel: 0,04 point) og PTSD-symptomer, med sammenlignelige bivirkninger og indlæggelser. Væsentligt kostede IM ketamin $647 pr. behandlingskursus mod $6.069 for IN esketamin, hvilket tyder på, at det kan være et omkostningseffektivt alternativ, der udvider adgangen til ketaminbehandling.

items.title: Real-world outcomes of intranasal esketamine and intravenous ketamine induction therapy for treatment-resistant depression in a community clinic: a retrospective cohort study.

summaries.en: Retrospective cohort study (n=63) comparing intranasal esketamine (n=37) and IV ketamine (n=26) for treatment-resistant depression in a community clinic. Both groups showed similar baseline depression severity (PHQ-9 ~18) and comparable improvements (mean reduction ~10 points). Response rates were 64.9% vs 69.2%, remission 32.4% vs 23.1%, with no statistically significant differences. Induction completion exceeded 90% for both groups.
summaries.da: Retrospektivt kohortestudie (n=63) sammenlignende intranasal esketamin (n=37) og IV ketamin (n=26) til behandlingsresistent depression i klinik. Begge grupper viste lignende baseline-depression (PHQ-9 ~18) og sammenlignelige forbedringer (gennemsnitlig reduktion ~10 point). Respons var 64,9% vs 69,2%, remission 32,4% vs 23,1%, uden statistisk signifikante forskelle. Induktionsgennemførelsesrate oversteg 90% for begge grupper.
